name: Cybersecurity Controls
description: A defensible cybersecurity control baseline as assessed in SOC 2, ISO 27001 and cyber insurance reviews: governance, identity, vulnerability management, configuration, data protection, network, endpoint, detection, incident response and third parties.
references: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST CSF 2.0, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, MITRE ATT&CK, CISA KEV

categories.name: Security Governance & Risk
categories.objective: Cybersecurity is directed by policy, owned by leadership, driven by risk and understood by staff.

items.control: An approved information security policy set is reviewed annually and acknowledged by all staff.
items.risk: Security expectations are unclear or unenforceable.
items.test: Inspect policies for approval within 12 months, and compare acknowledgement records to the active headcount.
evidence: Policy set with approval dates and version history
Acknowledgement completion report compared to the HR roster

items.control: The CISO reports security posture, top risks and metrics to executive leadership and the board at least quarterly.
items.risk: Leadership is unaware of cyber risk and under-invests.
items.test: Inspect board or risk committee packs for each quarter, and confirm they include risk posture, metrics and decisions requested.
evidence: Quarterly board or committee security reports

items.control: A cyber risk assessment is performed annually and on major change, with treatment plans tracked.
items.risk: Security spend is not targeted at the most significant threats.
items.test: Inspect the latest assessment for date, scope and methodology, and confirm High risks have treatment plans with owners.
evidence: Risk register entries with treatment plans

items.control: Staff complete security awareness training at hire and annually, and monthly phishing simulations trigger remedial training for repeat clickers.
items.risk: Staff fall for phishing and social engineering.
items.test: Compare training completion to the HR roster, and inspect phishing simulation results and remedial training assignments.
evidence: Training completion report compared to the HR roster (e.g. KnowBe4, Proofpoint)
Phishing simulation click and report rates by month
Remedial training assignments for repeat clickers

items.control: Staff and contractors are background-screened before access is granted, and their agreements include confidentiality and security obligations.
items.risk: Untrustworthy individuals gain access to systems and data.
items.test: For 25 new hires, confirm screening was completed before the system access date and that signed agreements are on file.
evidence: Comparison of access grant date to screening date

categories.name: Identity & Access Control
categories.objective: Only verified, authorised identities can access systems, with the least privilege they need.

items.control: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2 or certificate-based) is enforced for remote access, email, cloud consoles and all privileged access.
items.risk: Credential phishing and MFA fatigue attacks lead to account takeover.
items.test: Inspect IdP authentication policies and exclusions, and compare the MFA method report to in-scope users.
evidence: Conditional access or authentication policy export with exclusions
MFA method registration report by user
items.other: CIS Control 6.3-6.5; CISA phishing-resistant MFA guidance

items.control: Enterprise applications use centralised SSO, and every user has a unique ID with no shared accounts.
items.risk: Activity cannot be attributed and access cannot be revoked centrally.
items.test: Compare the application inventory to SSO-integrated apps, and inspect the shared-account exception register.
evidence: SSO application list compared to the application inventory
Shared account exception register with compensating controls
Local account listing for sampled applications

items.control: Joiner, mover and leaver events flow automatically from the HR system to the IdP, and leavers are disabled the same day.
items.risk: Former staff keep access, and movers accumulate access.
items.test: For 25 leavers, compare HR termination date to IdP disable time, and inspect HR-to-IdP provisioning configuration.
evidence: HR-to-IdP provisioning configuration (e.g. Workday to Okta or Entra ID)

items.control: Access follows role-based least privilege and is recertified quarterly for sensitive systems.
items.risk: Excess access increases the damage from a compromised account.
items.test: For sampled sensitive systems, inspect the review population, reviewer sign-off and completed removals.

items.control: Privileged access uses separate admin accounts with just-in-time elevation, a vault and session recording.
items.risk: Standing admin rights are abused or stolen for full compromise.
items.test: Inspect standing membership of privileged groups and cloud admin roles, and PAM or PIM configuration and session logs.
evidence: Privileged group and role membership exports
PAM or PIM configuration (e.g. CyberArk, Entra PIM)

items.control: Accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled automatically.
items.risk: Dormant accounts are taken over unnoticed.
items.test: Run an inactivity query against the directory and confirm no enabled accounts exceed 45 days without an exception.
evidence: Directory query results for last logon
Exceptions for service or break-glass accounts

items.control: Secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords) are stored in a vault with rotation, and repositories are scanned for hard-coded secrets.
items.risk: Leaked secrets give attackers direct access to systems and data.
items.test: Inspect secrets-scanning results and push-protection settings, and confirm rotation dates for a sample of vault secrets.
evidence: Secrets scanning results and push protection settings (e.g. GitHub Advanced Security, GitGuardian)

categories.name: Asset & Vulnerability Management
categories.objective: Every asset is known and patched against known vulnerabilities within risk-based timelines.

items.control: An enterprise asset inventory is maintained through automated discovery, and unauthorised devices are removed or quarantined.
items.risk: Unknown assets are left unprotected and become entry points.
items.test: Compare discovery output to the inventory and EDR coverage, and investigate unmatched devices.
evidence: Discovery compared to EDR and MDM coverage reconciliation

items.control: A software inventory is maintained, and unauthorised or end-of-life software is blocked or removed.
items.risk: Unvetted or unsupported software introduces vulnerabilities.
items.test: Inspect the software inventory for unauthorised and EOL titles, and confirm remediation or exceptions.

items.control: Authenticated vulnerability scans cover all internal assets monthly and external-facing assets weekly.
items.risk: Exploitable weaknesses go undetected.
items.test: Compare scanned assets to the inventory to measure coverage, and confirm authenticated scan success rates.
evidence: Scan schedule and coverage compared to inventory (e.g. Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7)

items.control: Vulnerabilities are remediated within risk-based SLAs (e.g. CISA KEV in 14 days, critical in 15 days, high in 30 days).
items.risk: Known exploitable vulnerabilities remain open long enough to be used in an attack.
items.test: Obtain closed and open findings for the period, calculate SLA attainment by severity, and confirm overdue items have approved exceptions.
evidence: KEV-listed findings and their closure dates
items.other: CIS Control 7.7; CISA BOD 22-01 KEV catalogue

items.control: External and internal penetration tests are performed at least annually and after major changes, and fixes are retested.
items.risk: Weaknesses that scanners miss are exploited by attackers.
items.test: Inspect the pen test scope, report and retest letter, and confirm high findings were closed.

items.control: End-of-life operating systems and platforms are tracked, and those that cannot be retired are isolated with compensating controls.
items.risk: Unpatchable systems are exploited.
items.test: Query the inventory for EOL OS versions and confirm each has a retirement date or isolation and an approved exception.

categories.name: Secure Configuration & Change Management
categories.objective: Systems, cloud environments and code are configured securely, and security-relevant changes are controlled.

items.control: Secure configuration baselines (e.g. CIS Benchmarks) are applied to servers, endpoints and network devices, and drift is detected.
items.risk: Insecure defaults and drift open attack paths.
items.test: Inspect baselines and the latest compliance scores, and confirm failed settings are remediated or excepted.
evidence: Configuration compliance scores (e.g. Intune security baselines, Qualys Policy Compliance)

items.control: Cloud guardrails (organisation policies, policy-as-code) and CSPM prevent public storage, open management ports and insecure services.
items.risk: Cloud misconfiguration exposes data publicly.
items.test: Inspect guardrail policies and CSPM findings, and confirm critical findings were remediated within SLA.
evidence: Guardrail definitions (e.g. AWS SCPs, Azure Policy, GCP Org Policy)
CSPM findings and trend (e.g. Wiz, Prisma Cloud, Defender for Cloud)

items.control: Changes to firewalls, IdP policies and security tooling go through change management with security review.
items.risk: Security controls are weakened by unreviewed changes.
items.test: Compare firewall and IdP audit logs to change tickets for a sample period, and confirm security approval.

items.control: The secure SDLC enforces peer review, SAST, dependency scanning (SCA) and infrastructure-as-code scanning in CI.
items.risk: Vulnerable code and dependencies reach production.
items.test: Inspect branch protection and pipeline configuration, and for sampled merges confirm review and passing scans.
evidence: Pipeline configuration with SAST, SCA and IaC scanning (e.g. Semgrep, Snyk, Checkov)

categories.name: Data Protection
categories.objective: Sensitive data is classified, encrypted, protected from leakage and disposed of securely.

items.control: A data classification scheme is defined, and sensitivity labels are applied automatically or by users to documents and email.
items.risk: Sensitive data cannot be protected because it is not identified.
items.test: Inspect the scheme and label policies, and review label coverage reports for SharePoint, OneDrive or equivalent.
evidence: Sensitivity label and auto-labelling policies (e.g. Microsoft Purview)

items.control: Sensitive data is encrypted at rest on databases, storage and endpoints with managed, rotated keys.
items.risk: Stolen disks, snapshots or devices expose data.
items.test: Inspect encryption settings for sampled data stores, the endpoint encryption compliance report and KMS rotation settings.
evidence: Endpoint encryption compliance report (e.g. BitLocker, FileVault)

items.control: Data in transit uses TLS 1.2 or higher, and weak protocols and ciphers are disabled.
items.risk: Traffic is intercepted or downgraded.
items.test: Run or obtain a TLS scan of external endpoints, and inspect load balancer TLS policies.
evidence: External TLS scan (e.g. SSL Labs, testssl.sh)

items.control: Data loss prevention covers email, web uploads, cloud storage sharing and endpoints for sensitive data types.
items.risk: Sensitive data is exfiltrated deliberately or accidentally.
items.test: Inspect DLP policies and a sample of DLP incidents for triage, and run a test transmission of dummy sensitive data.
evidence: DLP incident queue with triage outcomes

items.control: Media are sanitised and data is securely deleted at end of life, with certificates retained.
items.risk: Data is recovered from disposed equipment or decommissioned cloud resources.
items.test: Trace a sample of disposed assets to destruction certificates by serial number.
evidence: Certificates of destruction listing serial numbers
Sanitisation procedure aligned to NIST SP 800-88

categories.name: Network Security
categories.objective: Networks are segmented, filtered and accessed securely.

items.control: The network is segmented to separate critical systems, user networks, OT/IoT and guest access, with default-deny between zones.
items.risk: Attackers move laterally from a single foothold to critical systems.
items.test: Inspect network diagrams and inter-zone rules, and test connectivity from a user subnet to a critical zone.

items.control: Firewall rules are reviewed semi-annually, and unused or overly permissive (any-any) rules are removed.
items.risk: Rule sprawl leaves unintended paths open.
items.test: Inspect the latest rule review and its removals, and query for any-any or unused rules.
evidence: Rule usage or hit-count report (e.g. AlgoSec, Tufin)

items.control: Remote access uses VPN or ZTNA with MFA and device posture checks, and no management ports are exposed to the internet.
items.risk: Exposed remote access and management interfaces are exploited.
items.test: Inspect remote access configuration and run an external port scan for RDP, SSH and admin interfaces.
evidence: ZTNA or VPN policy with MFA and posture checks
External attack surface scan for exposed management ports

items.control: DNS and web filtering block known-malicious, newly registered and uncategorised domains.
items.risk: Users reach phishing and malware sites, and malware calls home.
items.test: Inspect filtering policy categories and attempt access to a test malicious domain.
evidence: DNS or web filtering policy (e.g. Cisco Umbrella, Zscaler, Cloudflare Gateway)

categories.name: Endpoint & Email Security
categories.objective: User devices and email, the most common intrusion paths, are hardened and protected.

items.control: EDR is deployed on all endpoints and servers in block mode, with tamper protection enabled.
items.risk: Malware and hands-on-keyboard attacks go undetected and unblocked.
items.test: Compare EDR coverage to the asset inventory, and inspect policy mode and tamper protection settings.
evidence: EDR coverage compared to asset inventory (e.g. CrowdStrike, Defender for Endpoint, SentinelOne)
EDR policy showing prevention mode and tamper protection
Sensors offline for more than 7 days report

items.control: Endpoints are MDM-managed, with full-disk encryption, screen lock, and no standing local admin rights.
items.risk: Lost devices expose data, and users with admin rights install malware.
items.test: Inspect the MDM compliance report and run a local administrators group audit on sampled devices.

items.control: Email is protected by SPF, DKIM and DMARC at p=reject, attachment sandboxing, link rewriting and external sender tagging.
items.risk: Phishing and domain spoofing reach users.
items.test: Query DNS for SPF, DKIM and DMARC records and inspect email gateway policies.
evidence: DNS records and DMARC aggregate reports
Email security policy configuration (e.g. Defender for Office 365, Proofpoint, Mimecast)

items.control: Office macros from the internet are blocked, and script interpreters and risky file types are restricted.
items.risk: Malicious documents and scripts run initial access payloads.
items.test: Inspect macro and attack surface reduction policies, and open a test macro document from the internet zone.

items.control: Removable media is blocked or must be encrypted, and autorun is disabled.
items.risk: Data is copied out on USB, or malware is introduced on removable media.
items.test: Inspect device control policy and exceptions, and test a USB device on a sampled endpoint.

categories.name: Monitoring & Logging
categories.objective: Malicious activity is logged, detected quickly and triaged around the clock.

items.control: Security-relevant logs from identity, endpoint, network, cloud and critical applications are centralised in a SIEM, with ingestion health monitored.
items.risk: Attacks leave no usable trail, or log sources silently stop sending.
items.test: Compare the SIEM source inventory to required sources, and inspect silent-source alerting.
evidence: SIEM data source inventory (e.g. Sentinel, Splunk, Chronicle)

items.control: Logs are retained for at least 12 months (90 days searchable) and protected from deletion by administrators.
items.risk: Evidence is unavailable for investigation or regulators.
items.test: Inspect retention and immutability settings and query the oldest retrievable event.

items.control: Detection rules are mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques relevant to the threat profile, and tested at least quarterly.
items.risk: Common attacker techniques are not detected.
items.test: Inspect the ATT&CK coverage map and the results of the latest detection validation (e.g. purple team, Atomic Red Team).

items.control: Alerts are triaged 24x7 by a SOC or MDR provider within defined SLAs and escalated per the playbook.
items.risk: Attacks progress overnight or at weekends without response.
items.test: Inspect SLA reports for the period, and for sampled high-severity alerts confirm triage time and escalation.
evidence: SOC or MDR SLA performance reports

items.control: Threat intelligence and vendor advisories are reviewed and actioned against the asset inventory.
items.risk: The organisation reacts late to actively exploited threats.
items.test: For recent high-profile advisories, confirm exposure was assessed and actions were tracked.
evidence: Threat intel sources and subscriptions (e.g. CISA, ISAC)

categories.name: Incident Response & Recovery
categories.objective: Incidents are contained, notified and recovered from, and lessons feed back into controls.

items.control: An incident response plan defines roles, severity levels and playbooks for ransomware, business email compromise and data breach.
items.risk: Response is slow and chaotic, increasing impact.
items.test: Inspect the plan and playbooks for approval within 12 months, and confirm contact details are current.

items.control: Tabletop exercises, including one with executives, are run at least annually and produce tracked improvements.
items.risk: The plan fails under pressure because it was never practised.
items.test: Inspect the exercise scenario, attendance and after-action report, and confirm actions were tracked.

items.control: A breach notification procedure meets regulatory and contractual deadlines (e.g. GDPR 72 hours, SEC 8-K within 4 business days of the materiality determination, HIPAA 60 days).
items.risk: Missed notification deadlines lead to fines and loss of trust.
items.test: Inspect the notification decision tree and regulator contact list, and for any notifiable incident confirm deadlines were met.
evidence: Regulator and law enforcement contact list

items.control: Forensic readiness is in place: evidence collection procedures, chain of custody, and an IR firm on retainer.
items.risk: Evidence is lost or inadmissible, and investigation is delayed.
items.test: Inspect the evidence handling procedure and the IR retainer agreement for current term and response SLAs.

items.control: Critical systems have immutable backups, and full recovery from ransomware is tested annually.
items.risk: Ransomware destroys both production and backups.
items.test: Inspect immutability settings and the latest recovery test report, comparing results to RTO.

categories.name: Third-Party Risk
categories.objective: Security risk from suppliers, SaaS and vendor access is assessed, contracted and monitored.

items.control: Vendors are tiered by data and system access, and critical vendors are security-assessed before onboarding and annually.
items.risk: A vendor breach becomes the organisation's breach.
items.test: For sampled critical vendors, inspect the assessment, SOC 2 or ISO certificate review and its date.

items.control: Contracts with critical vendors include security requirements, breach notification within 72 hours or less, audit rights and data return or deletion.
items.risk: The organisation cannot compel security or timely notification from vendors.
items.test: Check sampled critical vendor contracts against the security clause checklist.

items.control: Vendor remote access is MFA-protected, time-bound, limited to required systems and logged.
items.risk: Attackers use vendor access as a back door.
items.test: Inspect the vendor access platform and confirm sampled sessions had approval, MFA and time limits.
evidence: Vendor access platform configuration (e.g. BeyondTrust, Zscaler Private Access)
Vendor account list with expiry dates

items.control: Security settings of sanctioned SaaS platforms (sharing, MFA, OAuth app consent) are monitored for misconfiguration.
items.risk: SaaS misconfiguration or rogue OAuth apps expose data.
items.test: Inspect SSPM findings or manual reviews for the top SaaS apps, and the OAuth app consent policy.
evidence: SaaS security posture findings (e.g. AppOmni, Adaptive Shield)
